```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r attach}
library(priogridR)
```

The foundation functions provide a consistent route from locations to cells,
from cells to geometries, and from incomplete observations to analysis-ready
PRIO-GRID panels. All functions accept a `priogrid` configuration, so the same
workflow can be used with alternative resolutions and extents.

## Configure a small grid

The examples use a deliberately coarse global grid so they render quickly.

```{r config}
config <- priogrid::pg_config(
  nrow = 18,
  ncol = 36,
  start_date = as.Date("2020-12-31"),
  end_date = as.Date("2021-12-31"),
  temporal_resolution = "1 year",
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

## Convert coordinates and cell IDs

`pg_id_from_coords()` assigns longitude-latitude coordinates to configured
cells. Coordinates outside a regional grid return `NA` by default.

```{r coordinate-to-id}
cells <- pg_id_from_coords(
  longitude = c(10, 20),
  latitude = c(50, 60),
  config = config
)
cells
```

Cell centres can be recovered in any requested coordinate reference system.

```{r id-to-coordinate}
pg_coords_from_id(cells, config = config)
```

## Create spatial geometries

Use `pg_geometry()` to create polygons for mapping or points for distance and
nearest-feature operations.

```{r geometry}
cell_polygons <- pg_geometry(cells, config = config)
cell_centres <- pg_geometry(cells, geometry = "point", config = config)
cell_centres
```

## Validate and complete data

Validation reports missing or unknown IDs, missing time values, duplicate
panel keys, and—when requested—absent cell-time combinations.

```{r validation}
observations <- data.frame(
  pgid = cells,
  year = c(2020L, 2020L),
  events = c(3L, 1L)
)

pg_validate_data(
  observations,
  time = "year",
  config = config
)
```

`pg_complete_panel()` makes missing combinations explicit. Fill values are
applied only to rows created by the function; existing `NA` values are left
unchanged.

```{r completion}
panel <- pg_complete_panel(
  observations,
  time = "year",
  cells = cells,
  times = 2020:2021,
  fill = list(events = 0L),
  config = config
)
panel
```

## Join variables safely

The default relationship is many-to-one: the right-hand table must contain at
most one row for each inferred grid-time key. State another relationship only
when it is substantively intended.

```{r join}
cell_attributes <- data.frame(
  pgid = cells,
  region = c("A", "B")
)

panel <- pg_join(panel, cell_attributes, by = "pgid")
panel
```

## Plot a variable

`pg_plot()` creates a `ggplot2` map and returns it for further customization.

```{r plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.5}
pg_plot(
  panel,
  variable = "events",
  time = "year",
  time_value = 2020L,
  config = config
)
```
